title: P17 first chain: the P16 wiring test and the P16 E1 mutation count were stale after P17 changed the code they read
what_went_wrong: p16_a_negctl.sh stubbed DBXML=true for the real tail of p14_edge_run.sh; P17 A1 makes the tail verify the xml restore with `probe`, which `true` cannot answer, so 6 checks failed (exit 3 instead of the expected codes).

p16_e_negctl.sh expected the restore-result mutation to apply at one site in the suite; P17 A6 added a second `print("restored" if ok else "restore-not-verified")` site, so the count check failed (2, want 1).
Reviewer-style observation (Astra v12, V10): the pin-case wiring test did not assert exit 3.
root_cause: Controls that read or extract the code under test were not re-run against the planned change before the freeze; I knew the tail would change but only grepped for the tail text, not for the tests that stub it.
detection: P17 chain step 1c/1d: p16-a-nc exit=1 (FAIL=6) and p16-e-nc exit=1 (FAIL=1) on the new bytes, while the P17 controls passed.
impact: No false pass: the controls reported FAIL. Test-script faults, not product faults; the first chain was kept as recorded (chain.log).

correction.applied: p16_a_negctl.sh: a DBXML stub that answers probe, and an exit-3 assertion on the pin case; p16_e_negctl.sh: the mutation count is 2 (R28 and R31). Manifest b (27 files), p17_chain_b.sh re-ran both on the final bytes.
correction.result: chain_b: p16-a-nc exit 0 and p16-e-nc exit 0 (evidence/p17/chain_b/)

rule: Before freezing a change to code that other controls extract or stub, grep the controls for the text being changed and run them once against the unfrozen bytes (a pre-flight run takes seconds).
